results.question: You receive two Visa card offers: Option A is free but charges 1.5% on every foreign transaction. Option B costs CHF 8/month but has zero foreign fees. You travel to Europe 2–3 times a year. Which do you pick and why?
results.answer: I would take the free option. I travel only occasionally, and I prefer to avoid a fixed monthly cost. With cash and my PostFinance card, I manage fine abroad. Paying CHF 8 every month does not feel justified to me.

results.question: Your bank sends you a message: your free debit card will be replaced by a new Visa card at CHF 5/month. You can opt out and keep a basic account. What do you do?
results.answer: I would opt out and keep the basic account. I do not see a reason to pay monthly for something I do not need. My current way with cash and e-banking works well. I prefer to keep things simple and predictable.

results.question: A new Visa card offers 1% cashback on all Migros and Coop purchases. The monthly fee is CHF 4. Would this change how you pay at the supermarket?
results.answer: No, I would still pay with my debit card or cash. The cashback sounds nice, but I do not fully trust these offers. I like to see exactly what I spend without extra conditions. CHF 4 per month is still a cost.

results.question: Which of these would make you most likely to get a Visa card: (a) 2% cashback, (b) travel insurance included, (c) no foreign transaction fees, (d) a CHF 100 welcome bonus?
results.answer: None of these really convince me. If I had to choose, maybe no foreign transaction fees, but I rarely need that. I prefer to pay directly with money I have. These benefits feel unnecessary for my situation.

results.question: You currently use Twint for almost everything. A Visa card promises the same speed but adds rewards. What would it take for you to actually switch?
results.answer: I do not use Twint, I mostly use cash and sometimes my debit card. To switch, I would need to fully understand how it works and be sure it is safe. Even then, I am not sure I would change. My current habits work well for me.

results.question: Have you ever been in a situation where Twint or your debit card was not accepted? What did you do — and would a credit card have solved it?
results.answer: Sometimes smaller places only take cash, so I always carry enough with me. I plan ahead and withdraw money once a week. I have not really needed anything else. A credit card would not have made much difference in those cases.

results.question: A Visa card gives you CHF 50 welcome bonus but requires CHF 6/month for 12 months — total cost CHF 72. Is that a good deal to you?
results.answer: No, that is not a good deal for me. I would end up paying more than I receive. I do not like these kinds of offers with conditions. It feels unnecessary and a bit confusing.

results.question: If a Visa card saved you CHF 15/month through cashback and discounts, but cost CHF 10/month in fees, would you see that as a net gain or still feel reluctant?
results.answer: On paper it is a small gain, but I would still feel reluctant. I prefer not to depend on such calculations every month. With cash and e-banking, I know exactly where I stand. That gives me more peace of mind.

results.question: What is the absolute maximum monthly fee you would accept for a Visa card — and only under what conditions?
results.answer: At most CHF 5, and only if it is very simple and clearly safe. No hidden conditions, no complicated features. Even then, I would think carefully before agreeing. I do not really feel the need for a credit card.

results.question: If a Visa card were completely free forever but offered no rewards, would you still get one? What would be the point for you?
results.answer: Maybe, but only as a backup, not for daily use. I would still rely on cash and my PostFinance card. The only point would be for rare situations where nothing else works. Otherwise, I do not see much benefit.
